rejected.title: Activity networks
card: In an activity network, each activity is an arrow labelled with its letter and time, and each node is an event. A precedence table lists the activities that must finish right before each one can start.
A dummy activity is a dotted arrow with zero time. It shows that one activity must wait for another, without adding any time.
Some, not all
use a dummy when an activity needs only some of another's predecessors. If C needs A, and D needs A and B, a dummy runs from the end of A to the start of D.
Same two nodes
two activities must not both start and end at the same pair of nodes, or they cannot be told apart. End one at a new node, then add a dummy from there.
rejected.remember: A dummy adds a link without adding time: use it for a partial overlap of predecessors, or to keep two activities off the same pair of nodes.

a.q: In a precedence table, Q and R both need only P, and S needs both Q and R. Why is a dummy activity needed?
opts: Q and R would share the same start and end nodes
S could start before both Q and R are finished
R would have to wait until Q is finished
The project would take longer to complete
a.why: Q and R both start at the end of P and both end at the start of S, so without a dummy they would run between the same pair of nodes. S already waits for both, because both arrows end at its start node, so S starting early is not the problem.
a.clue: Without a dummy, where do Q and R begin and end?

b.q: Wen builds a deck. A clear site and B order timber have no predecessors. C dig holes needs A. D lay frame needs A and B. E fix boards needs C and D. How many dummy activities are needed?
opts: One
None
Two
Three
b.why: D needs A and B but C needs only A, so one dummy runs from the end of A to the start of D. C and D both end at the start of E, but they start at different nodes, so they do not share a pair of nodes and no second dummy is needed.
b.clue: Check both reasons for a dummy, one at a time.

draft.title: Activity networks
card: In an activity network, each activity is an arrow and each node is an event. Each arrow is labelled with its activity and its time.
A precedence table lists the activities that must be finished before each one can start. Read the table and draw the arrows in that order.
A dummy activity is a dotted arrow with zero time. It is used when an activity needs some, but not all, of the activities that another activity needs.
Example: A and B have no predecessors, C needs A, and D needs A and B. Draw a dummy from the end of A to the start of D, so that D waits for both A and B but C waits only for A.
draft.remember: The table says what must come first. A dummy adds a link without adding time.

a.q: P and Q have no predecessors, R needs P, and S needs P and Q. Where is a dummy activity needed?
opts: From the end of P to the start of S
From the end of Q to the start of R
From the end of R to the start of S
From the end of S to the start of R
a.why: S needs P and Q, but R needs only P. A dummy from the end of P to the start of S links them. A dummy from Q to R would wrongly make R wait for Q.
a.clue: Which activity needs more than its neighbour does?

b.q: Wen builds a deck. A clear site and B order timber have no predecessors. C dig holes needs A. D lay frame needs A and B. E fix boards needs C and D. How many dummy activities are needed?
opts: One
None
Two
Three
b.why: D needs A and B but C needs only A, so one dummy is needed from A to D. E needs both C and D, so C and D can end at the same event. No second dummy is needed.
b.clue: Check each activity: does it need only some of another's predecessors?

a.best: From the end of P to the start of S

problems.detail: Question a is the card's worked example with the letters changed (A, B, C, D become P, Q, R, S), so students can answer by matching the pattern rather than understanding when a dummy is needed.

The card says a dummy 'is used when' an activity needs some but not all of another's predecessors, as if that were its only use. In VCE networks, dummies are also used so that two activities do not share the same start and end nodes.
